text: Final categorization: OK (Justification: This is an original research article focused on the valuation of ecosystem services in Afghanistan based on land-use/land-cover (LULC) change. The study explicitly implements a national-scale spatial analysis covering the entire country of Afghanistan. It uses high-resolution LULC data (GlobeLand30) for 2000, 2010, and 2020, and applies spatial regression and the Dynamic Land System (DLS) model coupled with linear programming to simulate future LULC scenarios for 2030. The study develops and compares three future scenarios (Business-As-Usual, Rapid Economic Development, and Environmental Protection), providing quantitative spatially explicit LULC projections validated with accuracy metrics (overall accuracy 89%, kappa 0.78). The output includes mapped LULC projections and predicted ecosystem service values under each scenario. Thus, it meets all core inclusion criteria: national-scale spatial implementation, primary focus on LULC prediction/simulation, multiple future scenarios with quantitative comparison, spatial modeling with accuracy metrics, and mapped LULC projections. It does not meet any exclusion criteria.)
